title: Viva Glint: import HRIS data through Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service
summary: Hold: the attribute-access and staging paths omit the required wizard choice of destination apps, and present a CSV example as a generic connector route. The roadmap facts and licensing are supported. Several smaller corrections should clarify navigation and differences between Microsoft's pages.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans HRIS connector imports into Viva Glint from Microsoft Admin Center.
claims.quote: Customers will be able to use various connectors to HRIS tools to import HRIS data into Viva Glint from Microsoft Admin Center.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-11-06T23:04:41.
Organizational Data Service centrally imports and manages employee data for Microsoft 365 and Viva, including Glint.
claims.quote: provides a centralized way to import and manage employee data for Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Viva experiences, including Viva Glint.

claims.claim: The Glint import documentation lists Workday, SuccessFactors, APIs, ADLS and file-based imports.
claims.quote: Flexible employee data ingestion through multiple import methods, including Workday and SuccessFactors connectors, APIs, Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS), and file-based imports.

claims.claim: Connection setup selects a connector and Viva Glint, maps attributes, chooses attribute access and begins validation.
claims.quote: Review the connection configuration, including the selected applications and services, reserved attribute mappings, custom attributes, and attribute access settings.

claims.claim: Imports support full and incremental types.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service supports two import types:

claims.claim: CSV defaults to incremental imports and lets the administrator select full imports.
claims.quote: Incremental imports are selected by default, but administrators can choose a full import instead.

claims.claim: Files up to 2 GB are supported.
claims.quote: Connectors support imports up to 2 GB.

claims.claim: Learn says overall ingestion takes a few minutes to up to three hours.
claims.quote: Overall ingestion can take from a few minutes to up to three hours.
claims.fix: Replace the timing sentence with: "The Glint import page says overall ingestion can take a few minutes to three hours; the CSV service guide allows up to 24 hours for processing, or 72 hours for the first upload, and up to three days for profile-store availability." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/org-data-service/import/import-orgdata, whose timing differs.

claims.claim: The Viva Glint integration is enabled by default for new customers.
claims.quote: For new customers, Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service is enabled by default.

claims.claim: Existing customers with employee data must complete one-time attribute-mapping onboarding before importing from the service.
claims.quote: Existing customers with employee data already configured in Viva Glint must complete a one-time onboarding process to map Organizational data attributes to Viva Glint attributes before Viva Glint can import employee data from Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service.

claims.claim: The feature is released in phases and the onboarding banner may not yet be available.
claims.quote: Organizational data in Microsoft 365 is being released in phases. If you don't see the onboarding banner, the feature isn't available yet in your tenant.

claims.claim: The get-started page labels the API connector Public Preview, unlike its other connector entries.
claims.quote: API-based Connector (Public Preview)

claims.claim: The get-started page names an Azure Blob Storage Connector whereas the Glint page names ADLS.
claims.quote: Azure Blob Storage Connector | Microsoft pulls your .csv file from Azure Blob using a Blob container URL you provide.

claims.claim: The Glint import page requires Organizational Data Source Administrator to create and manage imports.
claims.quote: To create and manage employee data imports in Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service, you must be assigned the Organizational Data Source Administrator role.

claims.claim: A Global Administrator assigns the Organizational Data Source Administrator role.
claims.quote: The Organizational Data Source Administrator role is assigned by a Global Administrator.

claims.claim: Viva Glint service administrators can also be assigned the data-source role.
claims.quote: Viva Glint service administrators can also be assigned this role when they need to configure employee data imports through Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service.

claims.claim: The get-started page says only Global Administrators and Organizational Data Source Administrators can upload data.
claims.quote: Only Global Administrators and Organizational Data Source Administrators can upload data.

claims.claim: The data-source role can upload, update and delete organizational data for specified applications.
claims.quote: Data upload and management: Permissions to upload, update, and delete organizational data for the specified applications

claims.claim: The data-source administrator can connect HRIS systems.
claims.quote: This admin can also connect to human capital management (HCM) systems such as Workday and SAP SuccessFactors

claims.claim: Workday and SAP SuccessFactors connectors pull data using supplied source-system credentials.
claims.quote: Microsoft pulls data directly from SAP SuccessFactors's public APIs using SAP SuccessFactors credentials that you provide.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft advises confirming approval for direct connections to Workday and SAP SuccessFactors.
claims.quote: Your organization has approved a direct connection between Microsoft 365 and Workday.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Public reserved attributes are shared with Profile and experiences including Microsoft 365, Copilot, People card, Viva Amplify and Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Public reserved attributes are shared with Profile and used by other Microsoft 365 experiences that consume Profile data, including Microsoft 365, Copilot, People card, Viva Amplify, and Viva Engage.

claims.claim: Non-public reserved attribute sharing depends on the data-source administrator's access choices.
claims.quote: Non-public reserved attributes can be shared with supported apps and Microsoft experiences based on the access chosen by the Organizational data source admin during connector setup.

claims.claim: Glint imports only attributes shared with it through connection attribute access.
claims.quote: Viva Glint imports only the Organizational data attributes that are shared with Viva Glint through the attribute access configuration for this connection.

claims.claim: A full import replaces the imported employee population.
claims.quote: Use full imports to replace the imported employee population with the contents of the current import.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Employees absent from a full import may become inactive depending on configuration.
claims.quote: Employees that previously existed in Viva Glint but aren't included in a full import may become inactive, depending on your configuration and import behavior.

claims.claim: Workday connector refreshes are full imports.
claims.quote: Workday: Every refresh is a full import and sends a full-import signal to Viva Glint.

claims.claim: Workday and SAP SuccessFactors schema changes automatically trigger a full import.
claims.quote: Any schema change for the Workday or SAP SuccessFactors connector automatically triggers a full import.

claims.claim: Other connectors require administrators to resend all employees after schema updates.
claims.quote: For all other connector types, after a schema update, administrators must manually send data for all employees through a new incremental or full import.

claims.claim: Multiple connector instances or types turn off automatic full imports to Glint through Workday and SAP SuccessFactors.
claims.quote: If your organization has multiple instances of the same connector, or multiple different connectors, automatic full imports to Viva Glint through the Workday and SAP SuccessFactors connectors are turned off.

claims.claim: Each connector can send data to only one Viva Glint instance.
claims.quote: If your tenant has multiple Viva Glint instances, each connector can send data to only one Viva Glint instance.

claims.claim: Multiple connectors can import data into Viva Glint.
claims.quote: You can set up multiple connectors to import data into Viva Glint.

claims.claim: A hierarchy derived from an attribute mapped to Microsoft_ManagerEmail mirrors Profile, so avoiding that mapping preserves a distinct hierarchy.
claims.quote: If the Viva Glint manager hierarchy is derived from a Viva Glint attribute that's mapped to Microsoft_ManagerEmail, the Viva Glint manager hierarchy mirrors the Profile hierarchy.
claims.fix: Retain the observation about Microsoft_ManagerEmail but remove "do not map that attribute if you want them to differ." Append: "The consumption page instead names Microsoft_ManagerID in its advice for keeping the hierarchies distinct." Both source pages are already cited.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The import is covered by a Viva Glint license or a Microsoft 365 license that includes Viva Glint, supporting the included model.
claims.quote: Viva Glint | A Microsoft Viva Glint license, or a Microsoft 365 license that includes Viva Glint

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The get-started page lists per-app licenses but no price or meter for the import itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service Viva Glint import pricing licensing meter. Opened get-started and import-orgdata; read the licensing table and connector guidance. No import price or meter stated there.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: This import capability is admin-opt-in because an administrator must configure an import connection before it imports data.
claims.quote: The following steps describe how to create a data connection in Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service, configure access for Viva Glint, and import employee data.

claims.claim: Completing onboarding automatically sets Organizational data imports to Yes.
claims.quote: After the onboarding process is completed, Viva Glint is configured to import employee data from Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service. The Organizational data imports setting is automatically set to Yes.

claims.claim: Disabling Organizational data imports stops imports and yields ORG_UPLOAD_SWITCHED_OFF.
claims.quote: When imports are disabled, Viva Glint stops importing employee data from Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service, and uploads return the ORG_UPLOAD_SWITCHED_OFF advisory.

claims.claim: Organizational data imports must be Yes for Glint to appear as a destination in the admin center.
claims.quote: This toggle must be Yes for Viva Glint to appear as an optional end point for your connection in the Microsoft Admin Center

claims.claim: A Viva Glint administrator completes schema mapping and enables Organizational Data Imports.
claims.quote: Complete Viva Glint schema mapping. Ensure imported attributes are mapped to the correct Viva Glint attributes. After configuration, enable Organizational Data Imports in General Settings > Technical Configuration.

claims.claim: The five required Glint attributes are Email Address, First Name, Last Name, Status and Employee ID.
claims.quote: including the five required attributes: Email Address, First Name, Last Name, Status, and Employee ID.

claims.claim: Custom attributes require a pre-existing Glint attribute with an exact, case-sensitive name match.
claims.quote: Viva Glint imports custom Organizational data attributes only when a corresponding Viva Glint attribute already exists and the attribute names match exactly, including letter casing.

claims.claim: Unmatched custom attributes are ignored.
claims.quote: If Viva Glint receives a custom Organizational data attribute that doesn't match an existing Viva Glint attribute, the attribute is ignored

claims.claim: Data connections exposes validation and import status, ingestion summaries and advisories.
claims.quote: Each data import is assigned a unique ingestion ID, and the validation page provides an ingestion summary and advisory details.

claims.claim: Import email notifications support up to 10 Viva Glint admins.
claims.quote: You can also configure email notifications for imports from Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service. Up to 10 Viva Glint admins can receive these notifications.

claims.claim: The Glint switch is at General settings > Technical configuration > Organizational data imports.
claims.quote: You can enable or disable imports from Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service at any time from General settings > Technical configuration.
claims.fix: Use "Configuration > Service Configuration > General Settings > Technical configuration > Organizational data imports" in controls[0].ui and the table. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/glint/setup/manage-general-settings, which gives the initial Configuration symbol and Service Configuration heading. The omitted symbol and heading are navigational omissions, not wrong printed steps.

claims.claim: No API for the Glint Organizational data imports switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Glint "Organizational data imports" API PowerShell enable disable; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "Glint" "Organizational" imports. Opened modis-data-consumption and manage-general-settings; results document UI, not a switch API.

claims.claim: Tenant role assignment is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Roles & admins > role > Add assignments.
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Roles & admins. ... Select a role name to open the role. ... Select Add assignments

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments assigns a role using principalId and roleDefinitionId.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
{
    "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.unifiedRoleAssignment",
    "principalId": "<Object ID of user or group>",
    "roleDefinitionId": "<ID of role definition>",
    "directoryScopeId": "/"
}

claims.claim: The Entra portal steps require at least Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Privileged Role Administrator.

claims.claim: After entering the service through Settings > Viva > Data management, the attribute-access path goes from Data connections > + New import > connector type directly to Choose attribute access.
claims.quote: Select a connector type. The following example uses CSV import. ... Choose apps & services ... Select the Viva Glint.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].ui.path and its table path with "Settings > Viva > Data management > Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service > Data connections > + New import > CSV import > Choose apps & services > Viva Glint > Choose attribute access". State in the note that this is the documented CSV example. The required destination choice cannot be omitted from the path; describing it only in the note does not supply the route. The Settings entry is supported by the already-cited get-started page, so the pre-check's missing Data management text is not itself an error.

claims.claim: Attribute access is configured per connection, per destination and per attribute, separately for reserved and custom attributes.
claims.quote: Attribute access is configured separately for reserved attributes and custom attributes. For each attribute, select the applications and services that should receive the attribute data.
claims.fix: Qualify the attribute-choice guidance and controls[2].note with: "These choices govern application-specific and custom attributes; the service's applications guide says public global attributes are automatically available to Profile and downstream apps." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/org-data-service/distribute/applications, which distinguishes public global attributes from the configurable ones.

claims.claim: No API for configuring connection attribute access is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Organizational Data Service "attribute access" "staging" API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Organizational Data Service" "attribute" API. Opened modis-data-import and import-org-data-api-call; results give UI editing, not an attribute-access operation.

claims.claim: The staging route goes from connector type directly to File upload, import method, and data staging > Data staging.
claims.quote: Select a connector type. The following example uses CSV import. ... Choose apps & services ... Select the Viva Glint.
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].ui.path and its table path with "Settings > Viva > Data management > Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service > Data connections > + New import > CSV import > Choose apps & services > Viva Glint > File upload, import method, and data staging > Data staging". State in the note that this route is the documented CSV example. The mandatory destination choice is missing; the service entry through Data management is independently supported by the cited get-started page.

claims.claim: When staging is enabled, an Organizational Data Source Administrator must explicitly approve the upload before it reaches Glint.
claims.quote: When the data staging option is turned on, the uploaded file doesn't flow to Viva Glint until an Organizational Data Source Administrator explicitly approves it.

claims.claim: Data staging is available for all connectors.
claims.quote: Data staging is available for all connectors, so administrators can review the actual data before it flows to downstream applications and services.

claims.claim: Learn does not state that the staging option is on by default.
claims.quote: Searched: "Organizational Data Service" "data staging" "default". Opened modis-data-import and import-orgdata; both describe turning staging on, neither says it is enabled by default.

claims.claim: No API for configuring data staging is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Organizational Data Service "attribute access" "staging" API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "organizational data" "staging" API approve. Opened modis-data-import and import-org-data-api-call; Graph results concern unrelated approval systems.

claims.claim: The Glint consumption page also gives Setup > Migration and imports > Organizational data in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: in the Microsoft Admin Center at Setup > Migration and imports > Organizational data in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The Glint consumption page says the integration is available to all customers, including GCC Moderate.
claims.quote: The Viva Glint integration with Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service is available to all customers, including customers with multiple Viva Glint instances, customers in GCC Moderate (GCC-M) environments
